groups.heading: UNION ARCHITECTURE
items: Articles 74-75: PM-led Council and collective responsibility.

groups.heading: STATE PARALLELS
items: Articles 163-164: CM-led Council and Assembly responsibility.
Articles 166-167: State business and information duties.
The architecture is parallel with bounded contextual differences.

stages.answer_line: “Cabinet government” may name the constitutional form, while “cabinet dominance” or “prime-ministerial government” are later analytical claims about the internal distribution of power.

stages.title: NOMINAL HEAD, REAL EXECUTIVE AND BINDING ADVICE

groups.heading: FORMAL AND REAL POWER
items: The PM and Council form the real political executive.
Policy authority carries Lok Sabha responsibility.

groups.heading: ADVICE RULE
items: The President may once require reconsideration.

groups.heading: BOUNDARIES
items: Underlying legality may still be reviewed.
Hung-House appointment and dissolution use convention and floor testing.

stages.answer_line: Courts may review the action on constitutional grounds while Article 74(2) protects the advice itself from inquiry.

stages.title: CLASSIC FEATURES AND COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY

groups.heading: SYSTEM FEATURES
items: Dual executive and majority or coalition rule.
PM leadership and possible lower-House dissolution.

groups.heading: COLLECTIVE RULE
items: Cabinet decisions bind all ministers publicly.
A dissenting minister must accept or resign.
Loss of Lok Sabha confidence affects the entire ministry.

groups.heading: INDIVIDUAL RULE / LIMIT
items: A minister may leave for misconduct or failure.
Individual departure need not topple government.
Fusion does not erase courts, bicameralism or elections.

stages.answer_line: The President is normally a nominal executive, but bounded discretion and information rights prevent the office from becoming constitutionally irrelevant.

stages.title: CONFIDENCE, DISSOLUTION AND CARETAKER CONVENTIONS

groups.heading: CONFIDENCE TEST
items: Floor test where majority is disputed.
Defeat on an expressly treated confidence issue.

groups.heading: LOSS AND TRANSITION
items: Constitutional head may assess a viable alternative.
Caretaker government preserves continuity with restraint.

stages.answer_line: In the Article 356 context, legislative majority should ordinarily be tested on the Assembly floor rather than inferred from subjective claims outside the House; proclamation material is judicially reviewable.

stages.title: CABINET, COUNCIL AND PRIME MINISTERIAL LEADERSHIP

groups.heading: COUNCIL
items: The wider constitutional ministry includes several ranks.
The Council is not identical to the Cabinet.

groups.heading: CABINET
items: Handles policy, legislation, budget and crisis choices.

groups.heading: PRIME MINISTER
items: Selects and allocates portfolios through advice.
Chairs Cabinet and leads the majority or coalition.
Connects President, ministry and Parliament under Article 78.

stages.mechanism_strip: The Cabinet Secretariat page accessed on 24 August 2026 confirms business-rule administration, Cabinet assistance and inter-ministerial coordination.
stages.answer_line: Article 123 permits temporary legislation when Parliament is not in session, but repeated or strategic ordinances can bypass deliberation and weaken legislative accountability.

stages.title: CABINET AND PM DOMINANCE: THE CAUSAL CHAIN

groups.heading: CONSTITUTIONAL BASE
items: Articles 74-75 place the ministry inside Parliament.
Confidence links survival to Lok Sabha.

groups.heading: AMPLIFIERS
items: Majority, whip and Tenth Schedule risk.

groups.heading: EFFECT / LIMIT
items: Constitutional sovereignty does not pass to Cabinet.

stages.answer_line: Cabinet growth can hollow out deliberation through fusion, party discipline and procedural control without making the executive legally sovereign.

groups.heading: RENEWAL

stages.answer_line: The constitutional remedy for executive dominance is renewed parliamentary capacity, not abandonment of responsible government.

groups.heading: ADOPTION
items: Responsibility preferred to greater fixed-term stability.
Cabinet form could accommodate plural interests.

groups.heading: PERFORMANCE
items: Continuity also rests on durable institutions.

groups.heading: VERDICT
items: Stable majority may still weaken scrutiny.
Reform Parliament rather than remove confidence control.
